source_text: This self-framing contrasts with activist terminology like "FGM/C" (female genital mutilation/cutting), which some organizations adopt to align the practice with global bans and WHO classifications, despite empirical surveys indicating that 75-85% prevalence among Bohra women involves primarily Type I procedures without widespread infibulation or extensive excision. [2] [18]
